policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads the singular 'all his host' in PSA.148.2, parallel to the singular collective in the preceding colon's 'all his angels'. The qere base r00 is plural (צְבָאָיו 'his hosts'), which the ASV renders as a plural elsewhere; the ketiv r01 צבאו is the singular 'his host' the English wording reflects. The number distinction in the ASV therefore selects the ketiv.
